Package io.sentry.time

Class Deadline

java.lang.Object
io.sentry.time.Deadline
@Internal public final class Deadline extends Object
A point in the future, measured on a MonotonicTicker.

Exists so that callers never do arithmetic on raw ticks. A tick carries no unit and no epoch, so spelling out now - then < ttl at every call site is where unit mix-ups, sentinels that happen to mean "boot", and wrap-unsafe < comparisons come from. Each of those is decided once, here.

  • Method Details

    • after

      @NotNull public static @NotNull Deadline after(@NotNull @NotNull MonotonicTicker ticker, long amount, @NotNull @NotNull TimeUnit unit)
      A deadline amount of unit from now.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if amount is negative. A deadline that starts out in the past is a sign error at the call site; passed(io.sentry.time.MonotonicTicker) says it deliberately.

    • passed

      @NotNull public static @NotNull Deadline passed(@NotNull @NotNull MonotonicTicker ticker)
      A deadline that has already passed.

      Saves callers from reserving a tick value to mean "not set yet": 0 is a real and very recent instant on a boot-relative ticker, so a field left at 0 reads as freshly set rather than as unset.

    • hasPassed

      public boolean hasPassed()

    • remaining

      public long remaining(@NotNull @NotNull TimeUnit unit)
      How much time is left, rounded up, or zero once the deadline has passed.

      Rounding up matters: callers schedule work for remaining() and then re-check hasPassed(). Truncating would wake them a fraction early, to find the deadline still standing.

    • isAfter

      public boolean isAfter(@NotNull @NotNull Deadline other)
      Whether this deadline falls after other.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the two were created from different tickers, whose origins are unrelated and whose ticks are therefore not comparable.
